chunks.text:
Hi Rabia,

Got to see you a lot more this year. The café seemed to go very well, you told me every time that we got a chance to. About a community spending their weekend talking to a stranger at a _stranger_ house (albeit regulars becoming familiar faces). You're building the second thing.

IRL reminded me a lot about what apps like 222 fail to achieve. These apps are essentially optimizing for matching, yet the distinction between matching friends versus potential dates are a big difference here. Friendship requires repeated, low-pressure contact both parties agree to: same couch, same corner, same people showing up. Whereas with dates people often look for aesthetics value to determine a valuable match. And you can't really engineer that into a singular algorithm to gather everyone in one evening just to exchange Instagram and never talks again.[^again]

[^again]: Funny that you wrote about this [today](https://rabiasohail.substack.com/p/serendipity-cant-be-crafted-by-an)

iirc David Spinks puts it well, where "we don't build community. we build containers where community has a chance to emerge."[^spinks] You can't force scenius into being, but you can not-kill-it.

---

Brian Eno coined the term _scenius_ to describe the intelligence of a scene.[^eno] The ecology of talent that emerges when the right people keep showing up in the same place. But the room needs someone to hold it. Someone to open the door, arrange the pillows, make the space feel safe enough that people stop performing and start connecting.

Priya Parker writes about how gatherings crackle when invisible structure is baked into them.[^parker] The labor is designed to disappear. You've succeeded when no one notices the work. But the work is still work.

I see you carrying that. The cognitive load of remembering who's coming, who needs what, who might connect with whom. The emotional labor of being the bridge between contexts. Granovetter called them bridges, the connections that span otherwise disconnected networks.[^granovetter] You're the bridge.

---

Parker has this concept of generous exclusion. "By closing the door, you create the room." Judgment about who belongs is protection instead of gatekeeping. The host exercises authority so guests can relax.

You're intentional. You're curating without making it feel curated. The apartment café works because it feels like a living room, and living rooms feel safe because someone lives there. The big comfy couch. The pillows. The regulars who develop confidence that translates into warmth with newcomers.

> And _you built it._

Maggie Appleton drew the cozy web, Venkatesh Rao's name for the spaces that exist outside the dark forest of public social media.[^appleton] Private Discords, group chats, apartment cafés. The places where people talk without performing for an audience. 56% of Americans had a third place in 2021, down from 67% in 2019. What you're building runs against the current.

I think that the goal of third space is non-capitalistic attribution of hobby. In a way algorithms promotes a sense of capitalistic contributions, given that they are _built_ to optimize for similarity. We all know, that community ::thrives:: on productive difference. The scene requires friction, contrast, people who notice things that you might miss. In a sense, homogeneity is comfortable and sterile.

Building something without needing it to scale, monetize, or justify itself through metrics. The return rate matters only because it indicates trust, and trust is what you're actually building.

I'm glad we got to see each other more this year. I'm glad you're doing this work, even when the work is invisible, even when no one holds space for the person holding space. I see it.

Keep opening the door.

[^sign]

[^spinks]: david spinks, ["how communities emerge"](https://davidspinks.substack.com/p/how-communities-emerge) (may 2024). i recalled it from one of his podcast appearances; the line is in this post.

[^eno]: brian eno coined _scenius_. the advice is kevin kelly's, from "scenius, or communal genius" (the technium, 2008): "when it pops up, don't crush it. when it starts rolling, don't formalize it. when it sparks, fan it."

[^parker]: priya parker, _the art of gathering_ (2018). generous exclusion as protection. the host exercises authority so guests can relax.

[^granovetter]: mark granovetter, "the strength of weak ties" (1973). a bridge is the only path between two otherwise disconnected groups, and granovetter's point is that bridges are almost always weak ties. the connector is the bridge.

[^appleton]: maggie appleton, "the dark forest and the cozy web" (2020), drawing yancey strickler's dark forest and venkatesh rao's cozy web (2019). the spaces outside public social media where people talk without performing.
